topic: The Sun's atmosphere is hotter than its surface
claim: The Sun's outer atmosphere, the corona, reaches millions of degrees, hundreds of times hotter than the Sun's visible surface at about 10,000 F, and scientists are still working out why.

beats.caption: HOTTER THAN THE SURFACE?
beats.vo: The Sun's air is hotter than its surface.

beats.caption: Surface: 10,000 °F
beats.vo: The Sun's visible surface is about ten thousand degrees Fahrenheit. That is already blazing.

beats.caption: Corona: up to 3.5 million °F
beats.vo: But above it floats the corona, the Sun's outer atmosphere, and it reaches up to three and a half million degrees. Hundreds of times hotter.

beats.caption: Heat should fade with distance
beats.vo: That breaks common sense. Move away from a fire and it gets cooler. Here, moving away from the Sun's surface gets hotter.

beats.caption: Still unsolved
beats.vo: Why? Nobody has fully solved it. It is called the coronal heating problem, and it has puzzled scientists for decades.

beats.caption: Parker Solar Probe flew through it
beats.vo: So NASA sent Parker Solar Probe to fly through the corona itself, and it is still collecting clues. Would you trust a spacecraft that close?

sources.text: NASA Science, Our Sun: Facts, https://science.nasa.gov/sun/facts/ (photosphere about 10,000 F / 5,500 C; corona up to 3.5 million F / 2 million C)
NASA Science, Parker Solar Probe, https://science.nasa.gov/mission/parker-solar-probe/ (flew through the corona, announced Dec 14, 2021; coronal heating is an open question)
NASA Goddard SVS, Discovering the Sun's Mysteriously Hot Atmosphere, https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/12903/
